clue.text: Diver's back-to-front converted stable area

indicators.note: the last letter of the stable-area word is shifted round to the front, converting it

parts.note: a mews is a row of stables round a yard

explanation.surface: Someone describes a diver's odd, reversed conversion of a stable yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-to-front converted' moves the final S of MEWS to the front. 'Diver' is a bird, not a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: The smew is a small diving duck, so a bird that dives for its food.

clue.text: Drink is evil? Not very when taken with old American marijuana

indicators.note: not very says the abbreviation for very is to be left out of the evil word

parts.note: vice is evil, wickedness
tea was old American slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A question about whether a drink is truly wicked when mixed with dope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not very' strips V from VICE, leaving ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a chilled beverage, often sold sweetened.

clue.text: Satellite's lowest orbit — one's immersed in chlorite mixture

indicators.note: one piece is dunked into the middle of the other, the mixed letters
a mixture means the letters of chlorite are blended into a new order

parts.note: one's read as one is gives I'M

explanation.surface: A chemistry-lab scene: somebody plunged into a chlorite solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', contracted to I'M; 'mixture' and 'immersed in' are the two operations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roche limit is the closest distance an orbiting body can approach a planet without tidal forces tearing it apart.

clue.text: Used to connect supporter with worker

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it, so a seconder or second is a supporter
a hand is a manual worker, as on a farm

explanation.surface: An instruction on how to link a backer with an employee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used' looks like a verb but is the adjective meaning not new.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods have had a previous owner, so they are not new.

clue.text: Hint: coarse, initially sexist, joke is finely drawn out

indicators.note: coarse suggests the letters of hint are roughed up into a new order
initially takes just the opening letter of sexist

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A tip that a crude, sexist gag ends up long-winded and laboured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coarse' turns HINT into THIN, 'initially' gives S, then PUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin-spun thread is spun out very fine, so stretched into slender strands.

clue.text: Clothes? Good to get attention

parts.note: to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Asking whether smart clothes win a person notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Gear is informal for clothing or outfit.

clue.text: Mash somehow gets stuck in opera singer's tongue

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are wedged inside the singer's name

parts.note: Kiri Te Kanawa is the famous New Zealand soprano

indicators.note: somehow means the letters of mash are put together in some other order

explanation.surface: Mashed potato lodged in a diva's mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: The opera singer is the soprano Kiri Te Kanawa, known by her first name. 'tongue' means a language, not the mouth part.
explanation.definitionFit: Kashmiri is the language spoken in the Kashmir valley.

clue.text: Conclude corporations must be on the rise

indicators.note: in a down light, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: corporation is jocular slang for a big belly, as is pot

explanation.surface: A business forecast that firms must be growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporations' means paunches, not companies; 'on the rise' turns POTS upward.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop is to end or finish something.

clue.text: Perhaps chrome is made primarily into very fine material

indicators.note: primarily takes only the first letter of made
perhaps hints that chrome is might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A claim that chrome may be turned into a delicate fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' is the anagram signal, and 'made primarily' supplies the opening letter, placed ahead of the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Micromesh is a mesh with extremely small holes, used in filters and fine stockings.

clue.text: Perform in between activities

indicators.note: in says the answer is lying inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An actor performing in the gaps between other events.
explanation.definitionFit: To enact is to act out or perform a role or play.

clue.text: Guard Nick gets a new top

indicators.note: the opening letter of the nick word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: to nick a criminal is to catch them

explanation.surface: A guard named Nick receives a fresh shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' is a verb meaning arrest, not a name. 'gets a new top' swaps the C of CATCH for W; the clue does not say which letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch is a sentry or guard, keeping lookout.

clue.text: Ones who admit having joint possession

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so those who own are owners
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: People confessing to having a cannabis joint on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests cannabis but is the hip; 'Ones who admit' plays on own as confess.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership is the state of having possession or title.

clue.text: As an old hand, reverse-called on a semiconductor device

indicators.note: reverse tells you the word for called is turned around

parts.note: rang means called on the phone
an LED is a light-emitting diode, a semiconductor

explanation.surface: A veteran phoning a manufacturer of electronic parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns RANG into GNAR. 'old hand' suggests a veteran but describes an aged, knotted hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnarled means knotty and twisted, as an elderly person's hands become.

clue.text: Cannabis with change of direction makes crystal, perhaps

indicators.note: right swapped for left is a change of direction, R becoming L

parts.note: grass is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: Drug talk: cannabis processed differently becomes crystal meth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change of direction' swaps R (right) for L (left).
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is a fine, clear kind of glass, so an example of it.

clue.text: Advance screening of power survey

parts.note: to review is to survey or look over

explanation.surface: An early showing of a report on electricity supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A preview is a showing of a film before its general release.

clue.text: Timing mechanism spacemen utilised when trapped by alien

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are caught between the letters of the alien

parts.note: ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

indicators.note: utilised suggests the letters of spacemen are put to use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Astronauts' clock used while held prisoner by an extraterrestrial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'utilised' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters are put to a new use. 'when trapped by' puts them inside the film alien.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapement is the part of a clock that releases the gear train in regular steps.

clue.text: Western baddie circle

parts.note: a heel is a cad or villain

explanation.surface: The villain of a cowboy film rides round in a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn or move in a circle.

clue.text: Fear inlet is engulfing city

indicators.note: the inlet word swallows the city letters

parts.note: an arm of the sea is an inlet
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Panic as the sea floods a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is sudden fright or apprehension.

clue.text: It makes a brief appearance when one snaps

definitions.text: It makes a brief appearance when one snaps

parts.words: It makes a brief appearance when one snaps
parts.note: in a camera, the opening that lets in light flicks open only for an instant as a photo is taken

explanation.surface: Something that pops up for a moment when a person loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snaps' suggests losing one's temper; it means taking a photo.
explanation.definitionFit: The camera's lens opening appears only as the shutter fires.

clue.text: Holy Communion finally secure

parts.note: pi is slang for pious or holy

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of communion

explanation.surface: At the end of a church service, something is made safe.
explanation.definitionFit: To pin is to fasten or hold something firmly in place.

clue.text: Swinger's nude antics, getting covered in fruit

indicators.note: the scrambled letters are enclosed by the fruit word

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

indicators.note: antics, capers, suggest the letters of nude are cavorting into a new order

explanation.surface: A naked swinger's capers end with them smeared in fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'antics' is the anagram signal and 'getting covered in' the container. 'Swinger' suggests a wife-swapper, not a clock part.
explanation.definitionFit: A pendulum is a weight that swings to and fro.

clue.text: Agree with the man entering the Church

indicators.note: the pronoun goes into the middle of the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
him refers to a man

explanation.surface: Consenting to a man joining the Church.
explanation.definitionFit: To chime with something is to be in harmony or accord with it.

clue.text: Net's used to contain short temper

indicators.note: the reworked letters hold the small word inside
used, as in put to work, means the letters of net's are rearranged

parts.note: wee is Scottish for small or short

explanation.surface: A fishing net that holds a tiny fit of anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short temper' looks like one phrase but splits: 'short' gives letters and 'temper' is the definition. 'used' is the anagram signal; 'to contain' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten is to temper or soften something harsh.

clue.text: Regarding union input involved with gangster

indicators.note: involved, made intricate, says the letters of input are tangled

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A trade union's contribution got mixed up with the Mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' turns INPUT into NUPTI. 'union' suggests a trade union but means marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptial means relating to a wedding or marriage.

clue.text: Bill's idiotic definition of steam?

definitions.meaning: a bill is a poster or placard put up for the public
a silly way to define steam is water that is not frozen, read as two words

explanation.surface: A man called Bill's dim-witted account of what steam is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name; it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice is a posted announcement, like a bill on a wall.

clue.text: State of old PM, being without police officer's protection

indicators.note: the old PM's name loses the letters around it
protection says those officer letters stand guard on either side, so it is the outer pair taken away

parts.note: Benjamin Disraeli was a 19th-century British Prime Minister
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A former premier left without a police bodyguard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being without ... protection' pictures the Detective Inspector's letters wrapped round the outside of the old PM's name, so they come off its two ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Israel is a nation state in the Middle East.

clue.text: Puma in north America number about a million after a time

indicators.note: about means the number word goes around the other letters

parts.note: a count is a number or total

indicators.note: after puts the million pair behind the time pair

explanation.surface: A cougar in North America, with a numerical tally of sightings.
explanation.walkthrough: COUNT goes 'about' A T and A M, the time pair first because of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Catamount is a North American name for the cougar, also called mountain lion.

clue.text: It's made to hold a medical patient, say

definitions.meaning: a container such as a suitcase or box exists to hold things
doctors call a patient under treatment one of their ...

explanation.surface: A device built to restrain someone in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A case is both a container and an instance of illness under treatment.

clue.text: Pine from lightweight transport with end removed

indicators.note: the vehicle loses its final letter

parts.note: a moped is a light motorcycle

explanation.surface: A tree yields a light scooter with its tip lopped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' suggests the tree; it is the verb, to languish.
explanation.definitionFit: To mope is to brood or pine listlessly.

clue.text: Medium body measurement not good fun

parts.note: M is the clothing abbreviation for medium

indicators.note: not good says the good letter is left out of the measurement

parts.note: girth is the measurement around the waist

explanation.surface: A medium-size waist measurement that brings no joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mirth is merriment, laughter and amusement.

clue.text: See 4
Members backing means of corporal punishment

indicators.note: backing means the word is run backwards

parts.note: parts are members of a whole, as body parts are members

explanation.surface: Club members supporting the return of the cane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' suggests supporting but reverses PARTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A strap is a leather belt once used to beat schoolchildren.

clue.text: Indifference of company led by international organisation

indicators.note: led by puts the organisation letters at the head

parts.note: UN is the United Nations
a concern is a business or firm

explanation.surface: Apathy shown by a firm run by a global body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company' means a business here, not companionship; 'led by' puts the organisation first.
explanation.definitionFit: Unconcern is a lack of interest or worry, i.e. apathy.
